follow-up time: Through pregnancy and up to 6 weeks postpartum
outcome: Maternal complications (e.g., shock, mechanical ventilation, septic emboli, noncardiac abscesses)
cohort: Pregnant women diagnosed with infective endocarditis (n=9)
finding: Intravenous drug abuse was identified as a growing risk factor for pregnancy-related infective endocarditis, which was associated with high morbidity and mortality rates.
mod_finding: Most women with infective endocarditis delivered vaginally (89%), with only one requiring an emergent cesarean section.
